To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mindfulness meditation has beneficial effects on well being and ameliorates symptoms of psychiatric disorders, and that these effects are mediated by attention regulation, body awareness, emotion regulation, and change in perspective on self.

mindfulness meditation has been shown to be beneficial in a number of psychological disorders and that the mechanisms through which it works include regulation of attention, body awareness, emotion regulation, and change in perspective on self.

mindfulness practice is a process of change that involves attention regulation, body awareness, and emotion regulation through the fostering of self-regulation, which in turn involves the development of a perspective on the self and the present-moment experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how mindfulness meditation exerts therapeutic effects, with the goal of contributing to the development of more targeted and more effective therapeutic interventions.

the question of how mindfulness meditation works on the basis of what we know about the nature of mindfulness, and the biological, psychological and social factors that influence the effects of mindfulness.
understanding the mechanisms through which mindfulness meditation shapes the brain and behavior and how these processes may be integrated into a comprehensive framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mindfulness meditation is a complex intervention that trains the regulation of attention and emotion, is based on an existential perspective, and is enhanced by the intentional cultivation of insight and compassion. How Does Mindfulness meditation Work? Proposing mechanisms of action from a conceptual and neural perspective.
mindfulness meditation is an attention regulation system with a wide range of effects on body, brain, and behavior, which are only partially understood.
mindfulness meditation is a multifaceted practice that impacts multiple levels of neural function, personality functioning, and interpersonal functioning (Baer, 2003).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mindfulness meditation is a multifaceted practice that impacts different components of emotion, attention, and consciousness, and it has different effects on different target modalities.

mindfulness meditation provides a way to cultivate self-regulatory skills, including the regulation of attention, emotion, and behavior, which has important implications for the treatment and prevention of various psychopathological conditions.

mindfulness meditation provides a framework for learning to manage emotional reactivity by developing attention skills and awareness of emotions, and that mindfulness-based interventions enhance the ability to manage affective dysregulation in everyday life.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mindfulness is more than a trend.
mindfulness practice appears to facilitate the development of a specific mode of consciousness—present-moment awareness—that is readily available in all moments of daily life.
mindfulness meditation is not a singular, monolithic practice with a unitary effect.
